la-municipal-officeholders.summary: This app names your city, town or village and not its mayor, council members or chief of police. In New Orleans and Baton Rouge the Parish card names the mayor and the council, and in Lafayette the mayor-president.
la-municipal-officeholders.why: The Secretary of State lists Louisiana's mayors, council members and police chiefs, and this app does not read that list yet. Many councils are elected by district, and only New Orleans's district map has been checked.
la-municipal-officeholders.wanted: Each city's and town's current council district map, as a map layer or a file of its lines, so that a member elected by district can be matched to the spot you picked.

la-parish-district-lines.area: Louisiana — the parishes whose current police jury or council district lines are not confirmed
la-parish-district-lines.summary: In 58 of Louisiana's 64 parishes this app names the members of the police jury or council but cannot show which one represents the spot you picked, because it has no confirmed map of the current district lines there.
la-parish-district-lines.why: The Census Bureau's map still carries older lines in most parishes and none for the New Orleans City Council, and no statewide map of the current ones has been found. Old lines would name the wrong member for many people.
la-parish-district-lines.wanted: Each parish's current district map, as a map layer or a file of its lines, or one statewide map of every parish's current lines from a state office.

la-school-board-members.summary: This app names your school district and not the people on its board.
la-school-board-members.why: The Secretary of State lists Louisiana's school board members, and this app does not read that list yet. It also has no map of the boards' election districts, so it could not say which member is yours.
la-school-board-members.wanted: Each school board's current election district map, as a map layer or a file of its lines.
